extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine-learning researchers and practitioners working with patent text and patentability prediction
extracted.subtask_description: A large-scale, well-structured corpus of English-language USPTO patent applications (2004–2018) intended to support NLP and ML research tasks such as patent decision prediction, subject classification, language modeling, and summarization. Emphasizes inventor-submitted application texts and rich structured metadata to enable studies of patentability at filing and concept shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (jurisdiction, time range, language)
rubrics_metrics.description: English-language patent applications filed to the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) between 2004 and 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset covers applications (not granted patents) in English across this 15-year window, giving temporal breadth for studies of trends and concept shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document version (inventor-submitted vs. granted patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUPD contains the inventor-submitted versions of patent applications—not the final versions of granted patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design choice allows study of patentability at the time of filing using NLP methods, enabling analyses that would be inappropriate if only final granted texts were available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale / size
rubrics_metrics.description: With more than 4.5 million patent documents, HUPD is two to three times larger than comparable corpora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large scale supports training modern ML models and generating robust evaluations across many tasks and subpopulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of rich structured metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset provides each application's metadata along with all of its text fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rich structured covariates enable new NLP tasks that leverage metadata variation, allow conditioning or stratification in experiments, and support explicit studies of concept shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-purpose task support
rubrics_metrics.description: HUPD is described as a well-structured, and multi-purpose corpus intended for multiple NLP tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and documentation should facilitate reuse across tasks rather than being narrowly tailored to a single benchmark; researchers can apply the corpus to various problem formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary classification of patent decisions (new task)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a new task to the NLP community—binary classification of patent decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper presents this task as a case study, demonstrating feasibility and showing how structured metadata enables explicit studies (e.g., concept shift) for decision prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-class classification of patent subject areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for multi-class classification of patent subject areas using provided text and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers can use text fields and metadata to predict subject-area labels; the dataset's breadth supports many topical classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset can be used for language modeling over patent application text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale, domain-specific corpora like HUPD are suitable for training or fine-tuning language models tailored to patent/legal technical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarization
rubrics_metrics.description: The corpus can support summarization tasks on patent application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of full text fields enables extractive or abstractive summarization experiments; inclusion of inventor-submitted versions affects the nature of summaries compared to granted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Code, data, and dataset artifacts are made available via website, GitHub, and Hugging Face Datasets links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public hosting of data and code facilitates reproduction of experiments, reuse by the community, and integration into existing ML pipelines.
